text: Paged for CheckoutHigh5xxRate. Checkout is returning 500s for about a quarter of orders. I'm IC; opening this channel.
checkout v2.14.0 went out at 13:52, a few minutes before the errors started.
Logs show 'connection pool exhausted: payment-client max=8' on every failed order. v2.14.0 moved the payment client to an async pool with a max of 8 connections, down from 64.
Decision: roll back checkout to v2.13.4. Dev, go ahead.
Support has 41 tickets from customers who saw an error page at checkout or were told their card was declined.
Rollback to v2.13.4 finished. Error rate is dropping.
5xx alert resolved. Orders are completing normally again. Moving to monitoring.
Why did this pass staging? Staging only runs 5 concurrent checkouts, so a pool of 8 was never exhausted there.

Action items: Dev adds a load test with production-level concurrency to the checkout pipeline. Sam adds an alert on payment-client pool saturation. Jules sends the follow-up email to affected customers.
Closing the incident. Postmortem draft due Friday.
Final count from support for yesterday's checkout errors: 63 tickets. Payments logs show 1,140 failed checkout attempts from 812 customers.
Paged: orders-db is at 498 of 500 connections and the orders API p95 is 4.8 seconds. Order history pages are timing out.
I turned on recommendations_on_order_page at 09:58. It queries orders-db once per line item on the order page.
pg_stat_activity shows hundreds of identical SELECTs from the recommendations widget. That matches Priya's flag.
The flag went to 100% of users at once; there was no percentage rollout.
Turning the flag off now.
Connections back to 120, p95 under 300 ms. Both alerts resolved.
Customers could still place orders; only order history and order detail pages timed out.
Follow-ups: Priya batches the recommendation queries into one query per order. Lena makes percentage rollout the default for new flags. I'll add a per-feature connection limit on orders-db.
Paged: TLS handshake failures on api.larkspur.example, almost every mobile app request is failing.
Gateway v3.8.1 just rolled out. Could it be the deploy?
No. The failures started at 09:00:40 and the deploy started at 09:12:30. The deploy came after the errors.
Found it: the certificate for api.larkspur.example expired at 09:00:00 UTC. The auto-renew job has been failing since September because its DNS API token was rotated.
Renewed the certificate by hand and reloaded the gateway.
Handshake failures back to zero, alert resolved.
Mobile app users saw 'cannot connect' the whole time; web checkout was not affected because it uses a different hostname.
Action items: I'll fix the renew job's DNS token and add an alert when any certificate is under 14 days from expiry. Lena adds a check that the renew job succeeded in the last 7 days.
Paged: search p99 is 3.9 seconds. Results are slow but still returning.
No search deploys today and no flag changes. CPU and memory on the search nodes look normal.
Index shard sizes look normal too. Nothing obvious in the slow query log.
Latency is back to normal on its own and the alert resolved. We still don't know what caused it.
Action item: Dev keeps per-shard latency metrics for this window so we can dig in tomorrow. Root cause still open.
Paged: 12,400 payment webhooks undelivered. Merchants are not getting payment confirmations.
The partner endpoint answers 429 Too Many Requests. v1.9.0 raised the retry ceiling and our retries are hammering it.
Paused retries for the partner; the backlog stopped growing.
Backlog is draining slowly, alert still firing. Handing over to the EU on-call; keep this channel open.
Customers report avatar uploads fail with 'something went wrong'. 17 tickets in the last hour.
media-upload returns 500 for HEIC images since v4.2.0 went out at 10:15; the new libvips build has no HEIC support.
Rolled media-upload back to v4.1.3.
Customers confirm uploads work again.
Action items: I'll add HEIC samples to the upload tests. Sam makes the upload error-rate alert page when it is above 5%.
Paged: fulfillment queue lag over 15 minutes. Shipping labels are being created late.
Lag alert resolved by itself. Watching.
It fired again. This is not transient.
At 18:30 I lowered consumer_concurrency from 16 to 2 to cut costs. Evening order volume is more than 2 consumers can keep up with.
Reverted consumer_concurrency to 16.
Lag back under a minute, alert resolved.
Action items: Lena adds a capacity check before changing worker concurrency. I'll make the lag alert wait 10 minutes before resolving so it does not flap.
